sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the western flank of the Serre Mts. and the Capo Vaticano promontory. This source is a low-angle, NW-dipping, fault almost at the southwestern end of the extensional axis that runs along the southern Apennines.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable concentration of damaging earthquakes in the the area. In particular, this region has been struck, from north to south, by the: 1 March 1783 (Mw 5.9, Calabria Centrale), 5 November 1659 (Mw 6.5, Calabria Centrale), 7 February 1783 (Mw 6.6, Calabria), 8 September 1905 (Mw 7.1, Calabria), and the 13 October 1791 (Mw 5.9, Calabria Centrale).
The catastrophic multiple earthquake of 1783 has posed several issues concerning the causative structure(s) of such a remarkable sequence. In fact, the 1783 seismic crisis is only one of the so many other damaging earthquakes that have occurred throughout the region, thus making earthquake geology a particularly arduous task, all the more complicated by the elusive geology of southern Calabria. One could say that too many earthquakes have occurred in "too little space", considering the size of earthquake faulting that could account for several M > 6 events, close not only in time but also in space. All these issues have led several investigators to study the complex seismotectonics of the region south of this Composite Source. Conversely, the region at hand has been far less studied.
In synthesis, the Upper Mesima Valley is a broad, slightly asymmetrical syncline bounded to the east by the abrupt escarpment of the Serre Mts. The source is bounded to the south by the Nicotera-Gioiosa Ionica Line, and to the north by the Stretta di Catanzaro. This is the locus of large important earthquakes, one of which belonging to the 1783 sequence (1 March).
The major portion of this Source has been associated with the 7 February sub-event of the catastrophic 1783 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenic processes in this region, the reader may refer to the relevant Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on regional geological data. Also the dip was based on regional geological data and geometrical considerations. Rake is indicative of pure normal faulting, based on regional geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
